name: Scientific enquiry planning and hypothesis testing

questions.q: What is a scientific hypothesis in the context of a physics investigation?
a: A testable prediction or proposed explanation for a phenomenon based on scientific reasoning
A random guess with no backing
A final proven law of nature
A list of lab equipment needed

questions.q: What name is given to the variable that the investigator deliberately changes or manipulates during an experiment?
a: Dependent variable
Independent variable
Control variable
Random error variable

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of keeping control variables constant throughout an investigation?
a: To make the experiment take longer
To ensure that random errors increase
To ensure that any change in the dependent variable is caused only by the independent variable
To eliminate the need for measurements

questions.q: Which term describes the variable that is measured or observed as it responds to changes in the independent variable?
a: The independent variable
The control variable
The apparatus variable
The dependent variable

questions.q: Why is it important to repeat measurements (take multiple trials) for each value of the independent variable in an experiment?
a: To calculate a mean (average) and identify or reduce the effect of random errors / anomalies
To use up extra time in the lesson
To make the data table look longer
To change the hypothesis

questions.q: What is an anomalous result (anomaly) in experimental data?
a: A result that fits the exact pattern perfectly
A result that does not fit the trend or pattern of the other repeat readings
The highest possible measurement on a scale
The average of three trials

questions.q: When planning a table to record experimental data, what must be included in the column headers?
a: Only numbers without text
Random symbols
The physical quantity name or symbol along with the correct unit in brackets (e.g., Length / cm)
Drawings of the equipment

questions.q: What type of graph is most appropriate for displaying continuous numerical data where both the independent and dependent variables are numerical?
a: A pie chart
A bar chart with disconnected categories
A labeled map
A line graph or scatter plot with a line of best fit

questions.q: What does a line of best fit on a scatter graph help a student determine?
a: The general trend or relationship between the independent and dependent variables
The exact brand of equipment used
The total cost of the experiment
The room temperature during the test

questions.q: What is the difference between random errors and systematic errors in experimental measurements?
a: Random errors are caused by faulty equipment that is always off by the same amount, while systematic errors fluctuate unpredictably.
Random errors cause unpredictable variations in readings around the true value, whereas systematic errors shift all readings by a consistent amount due to calibration issues.
Systematic errors do not exist in physics.
Random errors can never be reduced.

questions.q: What does it mean for an experiment or measurement to be described as 'reliable'?
a: It was performed by a teacher
It took less than five minutes
Repeated measurements yield consistent, similar results
It used digital sensors instead of rulers

questions.q: What is the definition of 'accuracy' in scientific measurements?
a: How close a measured value is to the true or accepted actual value
How many times an experiment was repeated
How fast the student wrote down data
How expensive the measuring instrument was

questions.q: When designing an investigation to test how mass affects the extension of a spring, what should be the independent variable?
a: The mass added to the spring
The extension of the spring
The length of the ruler
The gravitational field strength

questions.q: In an experiment investigating how wire length affects electrical resistance, which factors must be kept constant (control variables)?
a: The length of the wire only
The material and thickness (cross-sectional area) of the wire, and its temperature
The voltage of the power supply and current simultaneously
The color of the insulation tape

questions.q: What should a student conclude if their experimental results support their initial hypothesis?
a: The experiment must never be repeated.
Science has ended.
The evidence supports the prediction, but further testing under varied conditions builds stronger scientific validity.
The hypothesis was proven to be absolute truth forever.

questions.q: What is precision in scientific data collection referring to?
a: Whether the equipment is digital
Whether the measurement matches the textbook value
How quickly the data can be collected
How close repeat measurements are to each other (small spread)

questions.q: Why is it good practice to choose a wide range of values for the independent variable when planning an investigation?
a: To reveal any trends, patterns, or non-linear relationships clearly across a broader spectrum
To make calculations more difficult
To use up all available weights in the lab
To ensure no anomalies ever occur

questions.q: What is a pilot experiment (preliminary testing), and why might a researcher conduct one?
a: An experiment flown in an airplane to test gravity
A small-scale trial run to check if the method works and find suitable ranges for variables
A final exam given to students
A test done without any equipment

questions.q: When drawing a line of best fit on a scatter graph, how should the line be positioned?
a: Connecting every single data point in a zigzag path
Drawn vertically from top to bottom
Passing as close as possible to all points, with a roughly balanced number of points on either side
Drawn horizontally across the middle of the graph paper

questions.q: What should a student do if they identify a clear anomalous result during data processing?
a: Include it in calculating the mean without checking
Erase it and pretend it never happened
Ignore it and never mention the trial
Check the procedure, re-test if possible, and exclude the anomaly from mean calculations

questions.q: Which of the following describes a continuous variable?
a: Time, temperature, or length, which can take any numerical value within a range
Shoe size or eye color
Types of metal (iron, copper, aluminum)
Pass or fail outcomes

questions.q: What is the purpose of evaluating an experimental method at the end of an investigation report?
a: To boast about how fast the work was done
To identify sources of error, limitations, and suggest improvements for future accuracy
To list the names of all lab partners
To change the hypothesis to match the errors

questions.q: If an ammeter always reads 0.2 A even when no current is flowing through the circuit, what type of error is present?
a: A random error due to blinking
A human reading error
A zero error (systematic error)
An anomaly caused by temperature

questions.q: How can parallax error be avoided when reading a liquid level in a measuring cylinder or a scale on a meter ruler?
a: Look at the scale from a sharp angle above
Squint your eyes shut
Stand across the room
Ensure your eye is positioned directly level with the meniscus or pointer

questions.q: What is a categorical variable in a science experiment?
a: A variable that describes types, groups, or categories (such as material type or color)
A variable measured in exact meters
A variable that changes every second
A variable with infinite decimal places

questions.q: When planning a fair test on how surface texture affects toy car travel distance, what must be controlled?
a: The mass of the car, starting height or release force, and ramp angle
The color of the laboratory walls
The time of day the experiment is conducted
The name of the student recording data

questions.q: What does a positive correlation on a scatter graph of two physics variables mean?
a: As one variable increases, the other variable decreases
Both variables remain completely constant at zero
As one variable increases, the other variable also increases
There is no mathematical link between them

questions.q: Why is it important to state the resolution of a measuring instrument (such as a 1 mm ruler vs a 0.1 mm vernier caliper)?
a: To make the report look more colorful
To show how heavy the tool is
To calculate equipment cost
To indicate the smallest change the instrument can reliably detect and measure

questions.q: What is the primary value of peer review or discussing experimental methods with classmates?
a: To spot flaws in the experimental design, control variables, or data collection methods that you might have missed
To copy someone else's homework
To argue about grades
To finish the lesson early

questions.q: If an experiment's findings contradict the initial hypothesis, what does this indicate in scientific enquiry?
a: The student failed the task completely
The experiment was a waste of time
The hypothesis was incorrect, which is a normal and valuable part of scientific discovery leading to new understanding
The measuring instruments must have broken the laws of physics

questions.q: How should you calculate the mean of three repeat measurements (e.g., 10.2 s, 10.4 s, 10.3 s)?
a: Multiply them all together and divide by two
Subtract the lowest from the highest
Add all three values together and divide by three
Pick the middle number only

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using digital sensors and data loggers instead of manual stopwatches in physics timing experiments?
a: They make funny sounds
They require batteries
They look modern
They reduce human reaction time errors and improve precision

questions.q: When writing up a conclusion for a physics investigation, what should be included?
a: A clear statement answering the aim, supported by patterns or trends in the processed data
A story about what happened during lunch
A list of every piece of equipment touched
An unformatted block of raw numbers

questions.q: Why is it important to use consistent units throughout all calculations and data tables in a physics practical?
a: To confuse the teacher
To prevent unit mismatch errors (e.g., mixing centimeters and meters)
To make numbers look smaller
To comply with art class standards

questions.q: What does an inverse relationship (negative correlation) between two variables look like on a graph?
a: A horizontal flat line
A line going upwards from left to right
A curve or straight line sloping downwards from left to right
A vertical circle

questions.q: What is the role of secondary sources (such as textbooks or verified scientific databases) in scientific enquiry planning?
a: To replace doing practical experiments entirely
To copy answers without thinking
To decorate lab walls
To research scientific background theory, expected values, and safety precautions
